Project PyrrhusKillzone 2: Unofficial PC Port (static recompilation)

A native Windows x64 port of the 2009 PS3 game, made by static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C ahead of time and compiled into a PC program; graphics go through Direct3D 12. No emulator runs at play time.

Status: Partly playable

You need your own copy of the game. This project ships no game code, data, assets or keys.

See the statusSource on GitHub

v0.1.6

30 Oct 2026 · pre-release

  • AddedMouse look: the mouse turns the view directly through raw input, with no acceleration or smoothing. Sensitivity, zoomed sensitivity and inverted Y are set in gameplay.ini under [mouse] (mouse_look, mouse_sensitivity, mouse_zoom_sensitivity, mouse_invert_y). The pointer stays inside the window while you play and is let go in menus, when paused, or when you switch to another window. It does not work in vehicles or on mounted guns yet. Only checked in scripted test runs so far, not yet by hand. Adapted from Project Helghast.
  • AddedThe first lines of the game's log name the port version, when it was built, its patch set and whether it is an installed or portable copy.
  • ChangedThe README is shorter: what you need, how to get it and the known problems first; the details moved to linked pages.
  • ChangedWith aim_assist = auto (the default), aim assist turns off while you aim with the mouse and comes back when you use a controller's stick.
  • FixedAfter updating over an older version, the game could keep using graphics pipelines saved by the older version, which lost the holographic sight's reticle and glow, some post effects and some models, and could run slower (#25, #27). The saved pipeline list is now tied to the build that made it and is discarded after an update, with one line in the log; the first start after updating builds them again and can stutter briefly. Shown in scripted runs under Proton with a deliberately different build's cache; not yet confirmed on Windows.
  • FixedA missing downloadable-content licence is logged in one short line.

v0.1.5

30 Oct 2026 · pre-release

  • FixedThe setup window keeps responding while it checks your game files, looks for your RPCS3, copies an RPCS3 save or asks GitHub for a newer version: these checks now run beside the window, with a short line saying what is happening, instead of holding it until they end (on a slow drive Windows could mark the window "Not responding"). The setup log gives each check's time. Refs #22.
  • FixedA rare crash in the main menu (about one start in twenty in our scripted runs under Proton): the SPU scheduler threads no longer use a Wine/Proton wait primitive that can corrupt its own wait list under load. No crash in 9 scripted runs since; not yet confirmed on native Windows.
  • FixedThe runtime's other timed waits (the game's system calls, the SPU runtime and the system libraries) no longer use that Wine/Proton wait primitive either; a stress test that makes the primitive fail within a second passes on the replacement. Not yet confirmed on native Windows.
  • FixedSPU interrupts that arrive back to back now resume the interrupted job with its own registers.
  • FixedYour own lines in kz2-install.ini stay: the launcher and the first run used to rewrite the whole file on every change, dropping comments, lower-casing keys and failing on a % in a path, a repeated key or a file saved in the Windows code page. They now change only the value they set; comments, the spelling of keys and keys they do not know stay as you wrote them. Tested with host tests.
  • FixedA disc ISO with the install folder on a FAT32 drive: the first-run build now stops before copying anything and says why (FAT32 cannot hold a file of 4 GiB or more, and the game's main archive is about 6.5 GiB), instead of failing part-way through the copy. Tested with host tests.
  • FixedThe setup and launcher logs also hide the user name in a Documents, Desktop or Downloads folder that Windows keeps outside your user folder (shown as <Documents>, <Desktop>, <Downloads>), in other accounts' folders (<user>), and in CMake's and URL-encoded forms of your user folder.
  • AddedEstimated hardware requirements to play and to build (README and docs/requirements.md): estimates, provisional until the game runs at full speed; hand play is not measured.
  • Added"Use my RPCS3 install" also finds an unzipped RPCS3 with its version in the folder name (such as rpcs3-v0.0.34-...-win64) in Documents, the Desktop and Downloads (also where Windows has moved them), Games or Emulators in your user folder, Program Files, and each local drive's root and its Games, Emulators, Emulator or PS3 folder, and accepts a picked config or dev_hdd0 folder inside it. One level deep only. Adapted from Project Helghast. Tested with host tests.
  • ChangedCorrection to 0.1.3's notes: zlib is linked into the game only when the build's compiler setup has it (our own Linux build). The first-run build of the installer and the portable zip has no zlib and uses the deflate decoder already in the runtime (from stb_image) for the same job; both decoders gave the same output in all 60 checks of our host test.

About the port

how it works

The port is built on ps3recomp (MIT): the PPU code and the game's SPU programs are lifted to C, the PS3 system libraries the game calls are reimplemented, and the game's RSX command stream is replayed on Direct3D 12. The game's archive is read in place from your dump. It is tested on Windows x64 under Proton.

It follows Project Helghast, the same method applied to Killzone 3, and reuses its general runtime work. More in the README.

Full status

Install

v0.1.6 pre-release

30 Oct 2026 · partly playable · Windows x64

Download v0.1.6All releases

The release page has the installer (recommended) and the portable zip, each with a .sha256 file, and SHA256SUMS: check your download against them.

The installer and the portable zip check your own disc dump, the 1.29 update and the decrypted EBOOT, then translate and build the game's code on your machine with a bundled compiler, with one progress bar and a full install log. Nothing of the game is shipped or downloaded; your dump is read where it is, never copied. What each input must contain: Getting your files ready.

Or build the port from source: building.

What goes online

Nothing unless you ask. The port starts no connection of its own; the version check and update download are off until you turn them on. Online multiplayer, if it comes, will only use a self-hosted server you choose. See the README.

Viewing this website loads the Rajdhani font from Google Fonts, which sees your visit; the repository, installer and game do not.

Requirements

What you need

ItemRequiredDetails
Operating systemyesWindows 10 or 11, 64-bit. Tested by us under Proton on Linux; players report playing on native Windows 11 (issue #13).
Graphics cardyesA GPU with Direct3D 12 support.
Killzone 2 disc dumpyesYour own copy of the US disc (BCUS98116), dumped to a folder or a decrypted ISO file (an encrypted ISO is refused); a FAT32 dump with the disc archive in parts is accepted as it is. Other title ids are refused, naming the id found; the Killzone Trilogy disc (its Killzone 2 is BCUS98116, disc version 02.00) is accepted as untested (what each input must contain).
Update 1.29yesThe game's last update, from your own console or copy.
Decrypted EBOOTyesThe game's main program (EBOOT.elf), decrypted, made from your own copy. This project ships no decryption tools or instructions.

Hardware to play

Minimum (estimate)Recommended (estimate)
CPUx86-64 with AVX and FMA3 (Intel Haswell or AMD Piledriver, about 2013, and newer; checked at start-up), 6 cores, about 3.5 GHz sustained8 or more cores, 4 GHz or more sustained, a recent desktop or laptop part
Memory8 GB (estimate)16 GB (estimate)
Graphics cardDirect3D 12 (an integrated GPU runs, slowly)a discrete Direct3D 12 GPU of the RTX 4060 / RTX 4070 Laptop class (8 GB), driver current
Disk spaceabout 12 GB free beyond the disc dump (estimate)the same, on an SSD
Operating systemWindows 10 64-bit, or Linux with a current ProtonWindows 11
Controllera keyboard and mouse (the default key layout and mouse look)a gamepad

Details: requirements.md. Hardware figures are estimates, provisional until the game runs at full speed; hand play is not measured.
